newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Uptrending T-bonds stall, await catalyst.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Uptrending T-bonds stall, await catalyst.

text.p: September Treasury bond futures remain on track to challenge 116-00 near term, but motivation was the missing ingredient Monday, some analysts said.

Futures traded at slightly firmer levels most of the day as market participants positioned for Tuesday's second-quarter U.S. employment cost index report, the first in a series of important releases scheduled over the next several sessions.
In addition to several second-tier reports coming out, the advance second-quarter gross domestic product will be released on Thursday and the July employment report on Friday.

If September bonds survive the potentially volatile week ahead with a close on Friday that is above last week's 1-1/2-year high of 115-23/32, the next leg up could extend to 116-28/32, said Bernard Savaiko, director of futures research for PaineWebber Inc.
"At that point, the market's getting up into rarified air," he said.
The analyst said strong data this week won't necessarily dissuade bulls who took encouragement from Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony last week.
"Greenspan indicated the economy is on strong footing, and he's not worried about inflation," Savaiko noted.
September bonds soared to 115-23 the day after Greenspan addressed the House but have been unable to build on the momentum, a fact that concerns some market watchers.

"We haven't gotten much ahead of where we were when Greenspan spoke on Tuesday," said Bruce Kamich, senior vice president at MCM Moneywatch. "If the market's going to do an encore, I don't know where it's going to come from."
Kamich predicted over the next two weeks September futures would retreat to 114-00 or lower, equal to roughly a 6.50 percent yield in cash terms, based on cycle analysis and timing models.
"Short term, the market has gotten ahead of itself," Kamich said.
He pointed out that open interest in the September bond gained about 30,000 contracts in the past week. "That's a lot of new people coming in at relatively high levels," he cautioned.
After a pullback, bonds would then be free to continue the trend on up toward 6.05 percent sometime between early September and mid-November, he said.

Greg Troccoli, director of technical trade strategy at Prudential Securities Inc, said a bullish flag formed on bar charts after the Greenspan rally, with Tuesday as the flagpole, suggests September futures are poised to challenge 116-04 at minimum.
A close below 114-24 would negate the upside target and redirect prices back down to 114-00, he said.
